content: Acidophilus refers to a general term for a group of probiotics that are often incorporated into milk or sold in capsule form. These probiotics contain one or more types of bacteria that play a role in aiding digestion. The specific bacteria included in these formulations are as follows: Lactobacillus acidophilus (A) Lactobacillus casei (C) Lactobacillus bulgaricus (L) Bifidobacterium bifidum (B) Streptococcus thermophilus Among these, only Lactobacillus acidophilus is considered the true acidophilus strain. However, many manufacturers, particularly in the United States, use the term acidophilus more generically to describe mixtures of bacteria, one of which is Lactobacillus acidophilus. Acidophilus can also be naturally found in certain high-quality yogurts and other traditional fermented foods. For more detailed information, it is recommended to review the individual bacterial strains and consult resources on probiotics.
